DESIGN STUDY: design and reference data only, NOT flight-certified. Not connected to any real vehicle or flight system. The flight profile is the speculative Pythagoras Concept Design v2.4 §4.7 profile.

Notes and assumptions

Positions are barycentric ICRS (ly) from the nav package. Between samples the display interpolates linearly; use navref for navigation-quality values.

Aim: the ship flies straight to the target's geometric position at arrival (intercept point). This includes the star's motion and the light-time correction. The target's motion during the flight (hundreds of AU) is far too small to see at this scale and is listed in the readout.

Gas clouds: Redfield & Linsky (2008) clouds on the sight line, projection only: there are no distances to cloud edges, so they are listed, not drawn.

Sky view: Hipparcos (ESA) stars brighter than Hp 6, plus the star-map stars within 50 ly, seen from the ship's current position, so parallax is included.

  • Aberration uses cosθ' = (cosθ+β)/(1+β cosθ).
  • Doppler factor δ = γ(1+β cosθ). Colour is a black body at δ·T. T comes from B−V via the Ballesteros 2012 formula, or from a nominal temperature per spectral class.
  • Black-body colours use the CIE 1931 fit of Wyman et al. 2013.
  • Brightness is scaled by δ⁴ (bolometric) and clamped for display. This is illustrative: the change in a real visual band depends on each star's spectrum.
